the addition of L- cystine to CHO cells expressing latent IFNβ increases the amount of correctly folded disulfide linked dimers and that the total yield of recombinant protein was significantly increased by co-transfecting a plasmid coding SV40 large T antigen.
we have shown that the expression of latent IFNB in CHO cells in culture can be improved by the addition of cystine and co-expression of the SV40 large T antigen.
the addition of L-Cystine to the medium increases dimer formation of the recombinant latent cytokine, while transfection of the large T antigen increases the total yield of recombinant cytokine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of recombinant proteins in CHO cells in a medium scale transient transfectant system.
the production of a recombinant protein in CHO cells in a biologically active, disulphide linked dimeric form.
the production of latent cytokine proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
L-cystine addition to CHO cell cultures expressing latent cytokines results in increased dimer production and total yield.
the expression of latent IFNB in CHO cells in culture is a feasible and practical method for producing this protein.
the addition of L-Cystine to the medium increases the proportion of dimeric latent IFN- β produced by the transient expression in suspension cultured CHO cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the expression of latent cytokines in suspension CHO cells is possible, but the production of the desired dimeric form is difficult to achieve.
the use of L-cysteine in CHO culture medium can be used to increase the ratio of dimer to monomer of latent IFNβ.
the addition of cystine to the medium can increase disulphide bond formation in the recombinant fusion protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ratio of dimer to monomer produced in the culture can be significantly altered towards increasing the dimer content by the addition of cystine to the CHO cell culture medium.
we can produce latent cytokine dimmers in CHO cells by transient transfection.
the ratio of dimers:monomers can be increased significantly in a recombinant protein by adding L-cystine, a disulphide reducing agent, to the cell culture.
